sermon.title: 70 Weeks Simplified Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor Kincer
sermon.summary: Comparing rapture charts, the teaching shows 69 weeks leading to the cross. God never wanted animal sacrifices; the Messiah confirms the new covenant. Daniel understood by reading scripture. The 70 weeks finish transgression and bring everlasting righteousness for every generation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Seventy weeks are determined For your people and for your holy city, To finish the transgression, To make an end of sins, To make reconciliation for iniquity, To bring in everlasting righteousness, To seal up vision and prophecy, And to anoint the Most Holy. “Know therefore and understand, That from the going forth of the command To restore and build Jerusalem Until Messiah the Prince, There shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; The street shall be built again, and the wall, Even in troublesome times. “And after the sixty-two weeks Messiah shall be cut off, but not for Himself; And the people of the prince who is to come Shall destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end of it shall be with a flood, And till the end of the war desolations are determined. Then he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week; But in the middle of the week He shall bring an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of abominations shall be one who makes desolate, Even until the consummation, which is determined, Is poured out on the desolate.”

chunks.short_answer: The Messiah—God promised a new covenant; confirm means proof; there is no added “he” for an antichrist.
chunks.text:
Let me submit to you. God promised a new covenant. Confirm means proof, evidence. Now, you’re going to tell me an earthly king is going to do something to prove that the new covenant has been initiated. No way. Only Jesus can come and prove by fulfilling all the prophecies. Just common sense tells you that. Isn’t that right? You’re looking at me kind of funny here. And in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and offerings to cease. Now the truth is a princely king did stop the Greek general did stop the sacrifices for a short season and the Romans did it in 70 AD and again in 134 AD and they haven’t been doing it since.

Animal sacrifices, the feast, the new moons, and the Sabbaths are an abomination to me. Why do people want to go back to the types and the shadows when they got the real thing is beyond my coranial understanding? It’s Jesus. This thing is about Jesus. This thing is about the Messiah. Don’t get hung up on the weeks and the years and the days. Everything in Daniel is pointing to Jesus Christ. And Gabriel is making it plain to Daniel what all the prophets said, what all his vision said about Jesus Christ. Can I hear him? A amen. Yeah. Now, for the overspreading of abominations and Jesus stopped the sacrifices and offerings when he died on the cross.

He was the one and only last sacrifice and offering. Ain’t that right? Isn’t that what the Bible teaches us? He stopped animal sacrifices. The shadow, the model of the real thing to come for the overspreading of abominations. He shall make it desolate. Okay? Because of sin, he’s going to destroy the Jews, their temple, their city, and their nation. Even until the consummation or the complete destruction and that determined, that officially decided on shall be poured out upon the desolate, which is the Jewish nation. Now the interesting thing here is all those white letters up there are not in the Hebrew Bible.

There is no he shall there. You just take those out and there is no pronoun he in the verses. And what is the subject of a paragraph? Is it the last sentence or the first sentence? Yeah. Who’s talked about first here? The Messiah. Who’s the most important thing that we need to focus on? The Messiah. Who conquers the prince of this world? The Messiah. Who cares about him? Why do we lift this guy up and call him the Antichrist, the beast, and the son of predition? Nowhere in Daniel does it say he is the antichrist. Nowhere in the Bible does it say the son of predition is the antichrist.

Nowhere. They just assume that when they talk. Nowhere in the Bible does it say the temple will be rebuilt again. Nowhere. But they have to have it rebuilt so that this mystical prince can stop the sacrifices again. The truth is this entire gap 7-year period of great tribulation theory is a major misconception and will probably go down in history as the biggest evangelical fundamentalist misinterpretation of scripture. Thus sayith Dave. As I read the Bible and studied it, I began to see what Jesus said about the end time. I began to see what scriptures clearly said about the end time.

And Jesus plainly said that as it was in the days of Lot and the days of Noah, so shall the coming of the son of man be. They were buying and selling. That’s tribulation. They were married and given into marriage. That’s tribulation. Some married people are nodding their head. Yeah. Yeah. I’m just kidding. They’re not nodding their head. See, they’re buying this. They’re eating and drinking. Eating and drinking. How many enjoy eating and drinking? Yeah. Pizza, soda. Yeah. Pasta. Yeah. That’s tribulation. But you see these people paint a picture of something so obviously eventful that no one in their right mind would reject Christ.

They want to sin and the Bible says, “No, you don’t have any special privileges.” That’s why religious people don’t like the Bible. And they want to come up with their own interpretation. Because they don’t want to be told how to live. And this is the very reason the Jews were punished twice. They were punished twice with desolation. Bible morality. Not their faith in God. It was their lifestyle, their moral choices.

You know, they had the responsibility to take the message to the world, don’t you? I don’t have time to teach that. But not just to serve God, but to take it to the nations. Yeah.
